messages:
Maya Patel: quick sync — BrightHealth asked for eval-triggered alerts + an Optimize advisor that recommends batching/caching/quantization defaults. They want a July pilot.
Samir Khan: got it. can we fold into next pilot slice? seems like two workstreams: alerts (signal + webhook) and advisor (heuristics + UI).
Jen Lee: prefer to split scope. alerts = eval hooks + rules + integrations. advisor = telemetry, heuristics scoring, and recommendation UX. different owners.
Ravi Kumar: FYI: alerting needs per-prompt eval hooks, a rules engine (thresholds, windowing), and retry-safe webhooks. advisor needs aggregated telemetry (latency, tokens, quality) + a small scoring service.
Alex Gomez: field note — BrightHealth cares about false positives and explainability. willing to pilot 6 weeks if FP < 5% and recs are actionable.
Maya Patel: propose launch criteria: 1) eval-alerts: validated on a 5k prompt set, FP <= 5% on customer vignettes, webhook with retry/backoff, and runbook. 2) advisor: produce 3 ranked recommendations (batch size, kv-cache TTL, quant profile) with simulated cost reduction >=10% on 2/3 workloads.
Samir Khan: effort estimate: alerts infra + rules engine ~3 sprints. advisor backend + heuristics + small UI ~3-4 sprints. shared pieces: telemetry pipeline and feature flags.
Jen Lee: recommend ship minimal alerts MVP first (simple threshold, webhook, enable/disable per-tenant). get BrightHealth feedback before advisor work.
Ravi Kumar: technical guidance — kv-cache TTL shouldn't be global. heuristic: if duplicate_rate > 0.2 and p99_latency < 150ms then recommend TTL up to 600s else recommend disable. quant gating: run a 100-shot eval; if quality_drop < 0.8% and latency_improve > 15% then recommend int8.
Alex Gomez: BrightHealth will supply a labeled eval set (2k) and 1-2 eng days for onboarding. they want canary rollout to 5% tenants and auto rollback.
Maya Patel: action items: Samir draft acceptance matrix by Wed EOD; Ravi prototype TTL heuristic and quant guardrails by Tue; Jen sketch alert UX + webhook payload by Fri. i'll coordinate legal/support.
Samir Khan: acceptance SLOs idea: alert latency <= 2s (eval hook to alert emit), webhook retry attempts 3, and alert precision > 95% on labeled set.
Jen Lee: UX note: alerts must include rationale (metric delta, baseline, example prompts) and next steps (e.g., "increase batch size to X", "enable quant profile Y"). include copy for customers.
Ravi Kumar: pseudocode for TTL heuristic: ```if duplicate_rate > 0.2 and p99_latency < 150ms:
  recommend_kv_ttl = min(600, duplicate_window_secs)
else:
  recommend_kv_ttl = 0  # disable``` Also quantify recommendation confidence; if confidence < 0.6 surface as "investigate".
ProductBot: :robot_face: created pilot "BrightHealth Optimize Pilot" assigned to maya.patel, samir.khan; target start 2026-07-01.
Maya Patel: risk note — ops/monitoring burden. add an "alert-suppress" per-customer flag and metric to track alert churn. include an ops playbook for noisy alerts and rollback.
Alex Gomez: field addition — need CSV export of alerts/recommendations for audit and RBAC to toggle recs.
Samir Khan: will include CSV export and admin toggle in acceptance matrix.
Jen Lee: timeline: slice A (eval-alerts MVP + webhook + runbook) = 6 weeks. slice B (advisor recommendations + UI + sims) = next 6-8 weeks. gating: BrightHealth sign-off on slice A required to advance.
Maya Patel: budget ask: dedicated eng allocation and 2 GPUs for quant sims for 2 months. i'll raise to eng managers today.
Ravi Kumar: engineering note: recommendations should include confidence, estimated cost delta, and automatic rollback suggestion (if applied automatically).
Alex Gomez: i'll confirm BrightHealth's labeled set timeline and pilot contacts.
Maya Patel: thanks team. reminders — Samir (acceptance matrix Wed), Jen (alert UX Fri), Ravi (heuristics Tue). i'll schedule pilot kickoff next week. :calendar:
